Rescue-Prime is a proof-system-oriented hash family with scheme-specific parameters.
SPDZ is a concrete actively secure arithmetic MPC family.
Revocation systems can use vector commitments or authenticated status lists for compact status proofs.

strengthens.notes: Domain separation makes transcript fields and protocol phases unambiguous.
Receipt-freeness and coercion resistance are stronger than ballot secrecy.

contrasts-with.notes: Deniable protocols avoid portable proof, while non-repudiation intentionally creates it.
PIR hides a database index, while PSI reveals an intersection or intersection-derived output.
SD-JWT provides selective disclosure, but not anonymous-credential unlinkability by default.

commonly-composed-with.notes: Accountability usually needs durable evidence and a review process.
Anonymous systems often need unlinkability across repeated actions, but the goals are distinct.
Audit trails are stronger when reviewers can independently verify records, proofs, or logs.
Threshold designs can remove single points of failure if quorum independence assumptions hold.
Encrypted mempools can reduce content-based censorship before reveal, but only under committee and inclusion assumptions.
FHE-based ML tooling still needs output, model, and repeated-query leakage review.
Most deployed confidentiality mechanisms also need tamper detection.
Key evolution and erasure reduce the value of later transcript compromise.
DIDComm is a wallet-agent messaging layer and should not be mistaken for credential privacy.
EUDI ARF profiles wallet roles, trust lists, and secure-device assumptions.
Forward secrecy is usually realized at the protocol layer.
Systems usually need both tamper detection and origin binding.
Signed evidence must feed a dispute or accountability process to have practical effect.
Threshold encryption can reduce pre-reveal content-based censorship but not all exclusion paths.
Context-bound tags prevent linkability across unrelated applications.
A verifier needs tamper-evident inputs and authentic verification parameters.

breaks-if.notes: Timing, network, amount, and rare-attribute metadata can defeat anonymity even when proofs verify.
Over-collected audit logs can defeat privacy goals even when evidence integrity is strong.
Sender, fee, size, and timing metadata can leave enough information to censor targeted users.
Confidentiality claims often fail operationally when encryption is used without authentication or plaintext is logged.
Publicly verifiable signatures on message content can create durable third-party evidence.
Size, timing, sender path, and censorship behavior can reveal transaction strategy even when payloads are encrypted.
MD5 is retained only for legacy recognition and non-adversarial checksum context.
Legacy RSA encryption can fail through padding-oracle behavior and should be isolated in migration inventories.
SHA-1 collision resistance is not adequate for new cryptographic uses.
Nullifiers deliberately create linkability inside a context and must not be reused across contexts.
Verification can be meaningless if public inputs, verifier keys, or context are omitted.

uses.notes: AnonCreds uses credential-specific ZK proofs and revocation registries.
arkworks provides implementation components for multiple SNARK constructions.
BBS-based credential profiles support selective disclosure and unlinkable derived proofs under pairing assumptions.
Circom circuits need explicit constraint review to avoid underconstrained statements.
EMP packages often depend on OT and garbled-circuit assumptions.
Threshold decryption distributes reveal power across a committee.
FRESCO is a framework layer; protocol selection determines the security model.
gnark circuit definitions must compile to constraints that exactly capture the intended statement.
halo2 is commonly associated with recursive proof-system engineering.
Encrypted mempools use commit-before-reveal or delayed-decryption sequencing rules.
MASCOT uses OT-based preprocessing for maliciously secure arithmetic MPC.
Microsoft SEAL exposes concrete FHE schemes whose parameter choices remain expert-sensitive.
MP-SPDZ exposes many MPC protocols with different adversary models.
OpenFHE supports several FHE families; guarantees depend on the selected scheme and parameters.
Shutter-style encrypted mempools use threshold encryption and key-release committees.
SLH-DSA SHA2 profiles rely on hash-based security assumptions and large signatures.
SLH-DSA SHAKE profiles rely on SHAKE-based hash assumptions and large signatures.
ECDSA data integrity credentials primarily provide issuer authenticity and integrity, not anonymity.
EdDSA data integrity credentials primarily provide issuer authenticity and integrity, not anonymity.
Orchard uses Halo-style proving to avoid the trusted setup model used by earlier Zcash pools.
Sapling is a concrete shielded-payment protocol suite.

weakens-if.notes: Setup or recovery ceremonies can become availability bottlenecks if no replacement path exists.
